name: Southern Ocean (Antarctic Peninsula)
blurb: Krill, ice and iron: a food web hanging on one small crustacean.

tip.title: Remove the krill
tip.text: Almost every predator here eats krill. Cut Antarctic krill by 80% and watch penguins, seals and whales feel it.

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Antarctic Peninsula, Antarctic krill, Southern Ocean). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.sp: diatoms living in and under ice

nodes.desc: Migrates to polar waters to feed on krill.
Top predator that includes several ecotypes. Some hunt seals and some take toothfish.
Pack ice grows from about 2.6 to 18.8 million sq km each year. Its underside grows algae and shelters young krill.
Weak in winter, then long summer days drive blooms.

nodes.name: Microbes
nodes.desc: Break down dead matter and return nutrients, including iron, to the water.

link_ideas.what: Humpback and blue whales migrate to polar waters to feed on krill

story: The Antarctic Peninsula is 80% ice-covered. Antarctic krill is one of the most abundant animals on the planet, about 500 million metric tons in all. Adélie and gentoo penguins, crabeater and fur seals, and blue and humpback whales all eat krill.
matters: The peninsula has warmed over the past 50 years. Sea ice has shrunk, ice-dependent Adélie penguins are declining locally and ice-tolerant gentoo penguins are increasing. Krill is also suffering from overfishing.
